newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU parliament rejects bid to sack EU commissioners.
newsitem.headline: EU parliament rejects bid to sack EU commissioners.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday rejected a demand for the immediate dismissal of European Commission President Jacques Santer and his 19 commissioners for mishandling the mad cow crisis.
As expected, a censure motion tabled by radical Belgian Socialist Jose Happart was thrown out with 326 members of the 626-member assembly voting against.

But a significant minority of 118, angered by errors the Commission made in fighting the spread of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) and determined to give Santer a warning, supported the move. There were 15 abstentions.
The motion would have needed two-thirds of the votes cast and an absolute majority of 314 votes in the assembly to be successful.

Happart, supported by a cross-section of small left- and right-wing groups, said the Commission had failed to give priority to the protection of public health and had caved in under British pressure to ease control measures.
He says the Commission also failed to carry out BSE inspections in Britain between 1990-94.
"The censure (motion) is the only instrument available to sanction the EU executive and force it to face up to its responsibilities and errors," Happart said.
On Wednesday, Euro MPs voted by an overwhelming majority in support of a resolution presented by the mainstream Socialist and Christian Democrat groups giving Santer nine months to put matters right.
Most Euro MPs feel it would be unfair to make Santer and his team, appointed in January 1995, the scapegoat for mistakes made mainly during President Jacques Delors's term of office.
